races.name: Carlsberg Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for David Weld with the yard in modest recent form (1 win from 10 over 14 days); only three career runs showing one place on similar going, but that placing came over 8f on Good — this trip up to 1m2½f is a step into the unknown.
runners_data.comment: Glittering Gem showed ability when third last time out, though she has been winless in recent starts and an unplaced effort sits between that and a seventh three starts back — a mixed profile. She has run over today's trip and going, and returns after 22 days off.

runners_data.name: Shemiyka
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for M D O'Callaghan, and the class standout on OR=120 in this field; held up last time on Soft 12f which flags a style inconsistency, and the drop to 1m2½f on Good suits better, but the racing-out-of-role flag (STYLE_FIT 0.90) should temper expectations if she cannot dictate cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts but shaped with some promise when third last time out; she has run over today's going before and a rating of 68 gives her claims, though five days between runs and 142 lb from stall 14 are factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up stayer for K J Condon with a strong record at this trip — five of seven career runs over 10-12f on Good, placing three times including two seconds; the Good ground is ideal and W J Lee's booking adds optimism, making him one of the most profile-suited runners to this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Taj Crown has been runner-up twice in her last three starts, showing admirable consistency, and has experience of today's trip and going — her rating of 71 marks her as a serious threat here. The risk is she remains winless in recent starts and must overcome stall 11.

runners_data.name: Capital Theory
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced 7-year-old for H D McGuigan returning after 288 days off; his one win came over 10f on Good going and he's placed on similar surfaces, but the layoff is a major concern and the 288-day absence makes fitness a genuine query.
runners_data.comment: Capital Theory showed real ability when winning two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going bolsters his claims at a competitive mark of 75; the chief concern is whether 288 days off the track has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Concert Party
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Denis Hogan with recent runs all on Good going, but all five recent efforts have come over longer trips (10f-17f) and his form figures in those races (5,9,9,7,9) suggest he hasn't recaptured the winning touch shown earlier in his career.
runners_data.comment: Concert Party won two of her last five starts, including a victory four starts back, and has experience of today's trip and conditions — a filly clearly capable on her day; the worry is her last two runs have both disappointed.

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: Winning hold-up horse for James Barrett who landed a 12f Good-ground race recently and ran second over 8f on Good; his true style is a deep closer but the crowded field has pushed him onto the pace map at midfield — he'll need a clear run late to show his best, and his STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects the compromise.
runners_data.comment:
Timandi showed good recent form with a win two starts back and a second last time out, and she has experience of today's distance and going; however, her inconsistency earlier in that recent run — including back-to-back unplaced efforts — suggests she can be hit-and-miss, making her a fair each-way proposition rather than a banker.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Jarlath Fahey who has placed on Good going (3rd, 8f) and was prominent in recent runs; a natural hold-up horse mapped closer than ideal due to field size, and the 52-day break adds a fitness question on what is only a fourth career start.
runners_data.comment: Avec Grand Plaisir ran third last time out but has been winless in his last four starts, and 52 days off the track raises a fitness query; he has run over today's distance and going, and draw three gives him a reasonable pitch, though his rating of 63 suggests he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Dark Summit
runners_data.note: Consistent back-marker for Denis Hogan who has finished in the top ten in every recent outing but shows a fade flag — the "000008" form string and six runs all on Good without placing tells its own story; genuinely needs everything to fall right late, and the field redistribution makes that even harder to achieve.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Dark Summit nevertheless carries strong ratings credentials as the top-rated runner in this field, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions. Drawn 16 carrying 133 lb, he was eighth last time out just eight days ago.

runners_data.name: Princess Rosie
runners_data.note: Returning after 317 days for P Cluskey and making her debut over this trip; all four career runs came over 7f on Good and she finished in the bottom half each time — the step up in trip is speculative and the absence is a major concern, especially with a claiming jockey.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for 317 days, Princess Rosie faces a stiff task from stall 5 off 133 lb; going experience offers a small crumb of comfort, but her recent figures make her hard to fancy at a mark of 57.

runners_data.name: Shay's Dream
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien-trained three-year-old on OR=120, but the "0-008" form string and four consecutive poor runs give little encouragement despite the class pedigree; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride which keeps him interesting, but the fade flag and lack of any recent placing make this a confidence-low profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with three unplaced efforts in that run and an eighth most recently, Shay's Dream is hard to fancy from stall 10 carrying 133 lb — though he has run over today's trip and going before, which is something.

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for John McConnell who placed twice on Standard going (3rd, 4th) and won once at 12f; wears a tongue-strap today, and while his history on Good going is mixed, the 24-day return and experience over this trip are mild positives in a wide-open field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn in stall eight carrying 132 lb, Chopsticks does have experience over today's trip and going, but a trainer without a winner in 30 attempts over the past fortnight is a significant concern for this lightly tried gelding.

runners_data.name: Eastern Blue Bird
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type for P A Fahy who showed a career-best placing (5th, 12f, Good) recently; the redistribution to midfield is a function of field size rather than natural style, and his Good-going record over 12-16f trips suggests the trip is well within range, though a 13-day turnaround is brisk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Eastern Blue Bird at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and a fifth last time out offers a faint uptick in form — though 132 lb from stall 13 makes life harder for a gelding rated just 59.

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Adrian McGuinness who won over 12f on Soft and has run on Good going multiple times; the fade flag is a concern and the 44-day break adds uncertainty, but the winning evidence over 12f trips at least confirms she can get the distance.
runners_data.comment: Three starts back she was a winner, but two unplaced-or-worse efforts since make her hard to fancy, and ranked 12 of 16 on our figures she faces a stiff ask off 132 lb from stall 7, despite having run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Michael Mulvany who races prominently — one of only two genuine pace horses in the entire field — wearing a tongue-tie and returning after just 12 days; his recent form shows a second over 10f on Good which is directly relevant, and his position tracking Shemiyka could prove a significant tactical advantage in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a second two runs back the only encouragement, Borora Aura heads into this ranked 14th of 16 on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, but stepping back into contention looks a tall order.

runners_data.name: Mullacurry Maid
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Donal Kinsella without a jockey listed at time of entry, wearing a tongue-tie; the fade flag is prominent and her form figures (17th, 5th, 9th, 8th, 15th) across recent starts on various surfaces paint a difficult picture, with no win from five and most finishes well beaten.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of poor finishes including a ninth and eighth, Mullacurry Maid looks a tough sell here; she has run over today's trip and going, and 27 days between runs at least suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Money Shuffler
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for W M Roper returning after 84 days, wearing blinkers; his entire form profile is on Standard going (STA) rather than turf Good, making the surface switch a genuine concern — all five recent runs came on artificial surfaces and his turf form is essentially unknown from this angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and returning after 84 days off, Money Shuffler does have experience over today's trip, though her recent form — a string of unplaced and mid-pack finishes — offers little encouragement, and 142 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

races.paceDynamic: Shemiyka is the one confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner field and, with Borora Aura the only other horse drawn to race prominently, she should be able to lead or sit just off the pace without being seriously pressured into a contested early gallop. On Good ground over 1m2½f at Sligo, that translates to a sustainable, controller's tempo — enough to keep the race honest but not a scorching early fractions that would suit pure closers. The absence of genuine rival pace-setters means Shemiyka can dictate terms and potentially pinch a winning advantage before the hold-up horses get fully organised. This shape clearly favours the prominent-racer profile: a horse that can track the leader at minimal cost through the race and pounce at the top of the straight, rather than a deep closer that needs a strongly-run race to generate a sustained late surge. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Dark Summit, Avec Grand Plaisir, Timandi, Chopsticks, Eastern Blue Bird and several others are natural hold-up types all competing for the same late ground, meaning most of them will be forced wider and closer than ideal, and only the sharpest of them can realistically secure their true running position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shemiyka Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Shemiyka leads uncontested and sets a comfortable pace that blunts the closers' momentum.
scenarios.body: Shemiyka dictates a sustainable gallop, and the hold-up brigade — crowded and unable to find clear runs in a 16-runner field — arrive too late; a horse racing prominently or just off the pace picks up the scraps as the field fans out. Borora Aura, sitting second throughout, and Taj Crown, who has a strong recent form profile in similar conditions, are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly more honest than expected and a gap opens late for a midfield tracker.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners funnelling into Sligo's tight home straight, a horse that travels smoothly in the first half of the midfield pack and finds a run at the right moment can deliver a sharp late challenge on Good turf. Timandi and Avec Grand Plaisir have the class credentials and recent form to capitalise if the race develops any real tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Shemiyka Leads All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If Shemiyka maintains her lead unchallenged through the home straight and the field simply cannot close.
scenarios.body: Given she is the highest-rated runner in the field at OR=120 and has only five days' rest suggesting peak freshness, if the pace is genuinely uncontested she retains enough class to hold on, despite the concerns about racing outside her natural prominent style. The crowded field behind her could create enough traffic to prevent a coordinated late challenge, gifting her the race on the nod.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Traffic, Wide Runs
scenarios.trigger: If the 16-runner field causes significant interference in the straight and the race breaks into scrimmage.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses all hunting the same late run simultaneously, interference and wide passages are a real risk, and the winner could emerge from an unexpected angle. Capital Theory won over this exact trip on Good going (OR=75, 1/10f/GOO in recent history) and carries experience that may allow him to find daylight when others are blocked.

watchPoints.text: Taj Crown (W J Lee) is the most tactically-positioned hold-up horse in the race — watch whether he gets a clear run into the straight, as traffic in a 16-runner field at Sligo is his single biggest threat to landing what looks a standout profile fit.

Borora Aura is one of only two horses likely to secure a genuinely prominent early position alongside Shemiyka — if he settles in second or third on the rail, he could be gifted a dream run that his modest OR=46 does not reflect.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Timandi, Avec Grand Plaisir, Dark Summit, Chopsticks and Eastern Blue Bird — will all be competing for the same limited running room in the home straight; expect at least one interference incident or a horse switched wide losing momentum at a critical moment.

Capital Theory's 288-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — D K Weld's stable is in better recent form and if Capital Theory is cherry-ripe on return (as the trainer's record with returning horses sometimes suggests), his 10f Good win in recent history makes him a pace-map wildcard worth monitoring in-running.

Money Shuffler's blinkers and exclusively Standard-ground form history warrant close attention in the parade ring — if he shows any signs of unsettlement on turf Good going, his already-modest claims are further compromised.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Connacht Oaks Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Alice Monet
runners_data.note: D K Weld's hold-up filly has won twice at this trip on good ground and her form figures over a mile and a quarter read well; the 313-day absence is the key risk, but Weld regularly produces horses fit first time back, and Chris Hayes's booking is a strong positive signal.
runners_data.comment: Alice Monet brings back-to-back wins in her recent form and has run over today's distance and going, while our rating has her clear of her five rivals — the lengthy absence of 313 days is the only query, though she lines up from stall 2 carrying 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Chica Guerrera
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner carries a 7lb claim for Reese Holohan and arrives just five days after her last run, which suggests Mark Fahey is happy she's bounced out of that effort; her soft-ground bias (1W2P on soft, 1W2P on good) is no real concern here, and an uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset.
runners_data.comment: Chica Guerrera landed a win two starts back and posted a third three starts back, showing consistent ability at this level, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions. The main risk is her unplaced effort last time, just five days ago.

runners_data.name: Cornelienne
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's five-year-old showed promise over staying trips including a Goodwood placing, but her last four runs have been over distances longer than today's 1m2½f and she has not run since February; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride, which is encouraging, but match fitness following a 203-day break is a concern she must overcome.
runners_data.comment: Cornelienne showed her class with a win and two minor placings in her last four starts, and her official mark of 92 underlines her credentials as a serious threat here; the main concern is a 203-day absence, which leaves fitness the key question.

runners_data.name: Spanish Temptress
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners a filly who has placed four times in six recent starts and clearly handles good ground, though she is a natural front-runner whose preferred position will be difficult to secure with Chica Guerrera taking the lead; the style-fit penalty means she is likely racing slightly out of her comfort zone whatever happens.
runners_data.comment: Spanish Temptress arrives in fine fettle — placed four times in her last six starts, including a win two starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions. The main risk is her rating of 88 against a 94-rated profile that suggests she may need to find more.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Kevin Thomas Coleman sends out a consistent handicapper who has been placed in 8 of her last 15 runs on good ground, but like Spanish Temptress she is a prominent type who will struggle to get that berth today; arriving just four days after her last run with her natural racing position compromised, the conditions here are working against her.
runners_data.comment: Thatwilldoso shaped well last time out and was a winner two starts back, but she ranks fifth of six on our figures and is hard to fancy at the bottom of the weights; the four-day turnaround adds a further question mark.

runners_data.name: Eastern Peace
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's hold-up filly has winning form on good going and at ten furlongs, and apprentice Patrick McGettigan claims 5lb; with only 13 days since her last run she arrives fresh enough, and as a genuine hold-up type she is perfectly suited to track a lone front-runner and finish through if stamina holds.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the six on our figures, Eastern Peace faces a stiff ask, with a fifth last time out and an unplaced effort two starts back doing little to inspire confidence — the trainer's run of 0/26 in the last 14 days is a further damper, despite her having distance and going experience.

races.paceDynamic: Chica Guerrera is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one rival likely to press from the front, she should be able to stride into a comfortable lead and control tempo on good ground over 1m2½f at Sligo. The pace she sets is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching — a measured gallop that keeps the race honest but does not burn off the field early. This shape classically suits hold-up horses who can track the pace from a distance before deploying their finish in the straight, and both Alice Monet and Eastern Peace, as natural hold-up types, are best positioned to exploit a race run at a controlled tempo. The field holds more genuinely prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Chica Guerrera has first claim on the front, while Spanish Temptress and Thatwilldoso, both true prominent runners redistributed to midfield on the map, are unlikely to get the spots they prefer and must race in an unfamiliar position, which blunts their effectiveness. The dominant shape here favours hold-up horses with stamina and class who can finish through from midfield-to-rear into a steady pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Chica Guerrera bowls along uncontested at a fair but unhurried gallop, setting up a true test of staying power.
scenarios.body: Chica Guerrera dictates from the front without serious pressure, and the race sets up perfectly for hold-up horses to pick off tiring rivals in the home straight. Alice Monet, with strong form at this trip and on good ground, and Eastern Peace, a hold-up type who stays well, are the profiles most likely to benefit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Nicks It
scenarios.trigger: If Chica Guerrera gets a soft enough lead and none of the closers can reel her in from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The pace is conservative enough that Chica Guerrera retains a decisive advantage into the straight and her rivals run out of real estate to close. Reese Holohan's 7lb claim is a significant weight-carrying advantage in a handicap of this nature and may prove the decisive edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Surprise Outcome
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the race turns into a rough, bunched affair with no true end-to-end gallop.
scenarios.body: Spanish Temptress and Thatwilldoso, forced into unnatural midfield berths, are unable to assert their natural forward prominence, creating a messy race where positional advantage is lost. Cornelienne, stepping back in trip with Dylan Browne McMonagle riding, could capitalise on a muddled tempo if she travels well from her prominent starting position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long-Range Hold-Up Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely quick early and the field strings out, demanding class and stamina over tactical speed.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong gallop burns off the mid-division horses and only the deepest stayer can close from the back. Alice Monet's two wins at this distance on good ground and her D K Weld handling make her the standout beneficiary, though the 313-day layoff is a risk factor that could blunt her response.

watchPoints.text: Alice Monet has not run in 313 days — watch her pre-race condition and whether she moves freely to post, as a stiff or unsettled appearance would undermine her chance significantly despite the obvious class.

Spanish Temptress and Thatwilldoso may both attempt to press Chica Guerrera for prominent position at the start — watch the first furlong for a potential positional battle that could compress the pace and produce an uncharacteristically fast early tempo.

Cornelienne's 203-day absence is the longest in the field — watch her market drifts close to post time as a sign the O'Brien team are uncertain about her fitness, which would make her outsider odds feel entirely justified.

Chica Guerrera ran just five days ago — watch for any signs of post-race fatigue in the paddock, as a horse who has not fully recovered from her previous effort would be vulnerable to being reeled in even at a sensible pace.

Eastern Peace's 5lb claim for McGettigan is live in a six-runner handicap — watch whether she travels smoothly in the hold-up position in the early stages, as a horse who fights for her head or races keenly would undermine the late-finish profile she needs to deliver.

races.name: John Gilligan Memorial Nursery Handicap

runners_data.name: Tatianna
runners_data.note: The only true pace-setter in the race; Good-ground form reads well (win and place on sim going) and she steps back to 6f after a 7f run, which may sharpen her; Josh Halley yard is 0/8 in the 14-day window but Tatianna's role as solo leader is the defining factor, not trainer stats.
runners_data.comment: Tatianna arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid grounding for this test; the main concern is whether she can reproduce that form from stall 11 carrying 143 lb.

runners_data.name: Hi Corbett Court
runners_data.note: W J Lee is an upgrade in the saddle for P Twomey's yard (3/15 in 14 days), and three prior starts have all come on Good ground with a placed effort at this exact 6f trip; a genuine closer who should get a clean run from the rear in a race where the straight suits a late run.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back gives Hi Corbett Court a form line worth noting, and he returns fit on 12 days' rest having run over today's trip and going before; winless in his last three, but his rating of 88 marks him as the one to beat from stall 1 carrying 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Two Brigade
runners_data.note: Held up and a little exposed after three starts (best of 5th), with a hood noted and the step up to 6f last time returning a modest 6th; Good-ground form is limited and the stable (1/11 T14) is running at a modest clip, making this a tough ask in a competitive nursery.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, Two Brigade has run over today's trip and going before, but his rating of 67 leaves him needing to find improvement; the 33-day break at least suggests connections have had time to work on his recent string of mid-pack finishes.

runners_data.name: The Drambling Man
runners_data.note: Consistent mid-table finisher (6-6-9-9) who has not threatened on Good ground across four starts; Rory Cleary's booking adds some interest for Kevin Coleman but the form figures offer no obvious angle for a race in which position will be hard to secure.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a pair of sixth-place finishes the best he can offer recently, The Drambling Man faces an uphill task here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 74 gives him a slight edge over his official mark, but consistency remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Fine Line
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's runner carries a fade-in-finish flag and has posted three consecutive zeros on Good going at trips of 6f-7f; genuinely hold-up in style but mapped to midfield due to field congestion — the poor finishing record in similar conditions makes improvement hard to project.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Fine Line faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a quick turnaround of just eight days.

runners_data.name: No Time Faults
runners_data.note: Three starts for Kevin Coleman all ended with double-figure finishes on Good ground, and the fade flag underlines a chronic inability to pick up in the straight; Leigh Roche can only do so much with limited raw ability here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, No Time Faults at least has experience of today's distance and going to call on; she carries 132 lb from stall seven, and while our rating of 74 suggests she holds some ability, those three recent unplaced efforts are hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Woodlawn Lily
runners_data.note: The only other prominent-style runner; Patrick McGettigan (5lb claimer) keeps the ride for J P Murtagh's yard (2/18 T14), and four starts on Good or Soft ground have produced placed efforts, suggesting she handles conditions; tracking Tatianna at the head of the field is her natural position and gives her a tactical edge over the closers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Woodlawn Lily nonetheless catches the eye on fitness — just 17 days since her last outing — and she has run over today's distance and going before, while our rating of 76 suggests she merits serious respect at this level; the risk is that her recent form has been consistently mid-division.

runners_data.name: Mr Montauk
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant jockey booking for Joseph O'Brien's yard (13/72 T14 — solid strike rate), and a placed effort on Good ground at 5f hints at ability; a true hold-up type displaced into midfield in this shape, so needs more luck in running than ideal, but the jockey quality keeps him relevant.
runners_data.comment: Ran a solid third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a strong platform to threaten here; the main risk is that he remains winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Stellar Path
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue strap, previously with hood) and three mid-pack finishes (8-8-9) on Good and Soft ground tell a story of limited acceleration; Gavin Ryan's booking is solid but the fade flag and modest form combine to make this a tough pitch.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with a run of eighths and a ninth doing little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp 17-day turnaround; at 125 lb from stall 13, she faces a stiff task to reverse that recent slide.

runners_data.name: Exchange Student
runners_data.note: Three runs have produced finishes of 15th, 11th and 7th on Good ground, so the trajectory is improving slightly but from a low base; a true hold-up runner condensed into midfield, and Andrew Slattery will need significant improvement to feature.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Exchange Student faces a stiff task from stall nine carrying 124 lb, and her ranking of 11th of 13 on our figures makes her hard to fancy — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs leaves her fresh.

runners_data.name: Ballymackney
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's yard (4/23 T14) sends out the biggest-distance dropper in the field — ran over 8f last time out — and the cheekpieces are a new addition; a hold-up type with modest form on Good ground whose best chance may come if the pace dries up and closers fire late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with an unplaced effort 13 days ago doing little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a drop to stall three could be worth noting — her rating of 66 suggests more ability than her recent form shows.

runners_data.name: Littlepacer
runners_data.note: A 7lb claimer for J P Murtagh (2/18 T14) aboard a horse who has finished 13th, 13th and 8th in three runs; the fade flag and consistently poor finishes on Good and Soft ground make it very difficult to construct a winning case, despite the promising stable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, all ending in defeat, Littlepacer faces a stiff task ranked 12 of 13 on our figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Sophia Royale
runners_data.note: Longest absentee in the field at 47 days off a first outing on Soft ground, with a best of 7th from three Soft-ground runs; Alan McIntyre's yard is 0/1 in the 14-day window and the switch to Good ground after exclusively Soft experience is an unknown, making her among the most speculative runners here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, the most recent an unplaced effort 47 days ago, Sophia Royale faces a stiff task here — our figures rank her last of 13, and while she has run over today's trip, there is little in recent form to inspire confidence from stall 12 off 119 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Tatianna is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner nursery field and, with no genuine rival to pressure her from the gates, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Sligo's flat 6f on good ground. Woodlawn Lily is the only other runner with a prominent tag and will likely track Tatianna, but she is not a natural pace-presser and should settle just off the leader rather than force the tempo up. The bulk of the field — Hi Corbett Court, Two Brigade, The Drambling Man, Fine Line, Mr Montauk, Stellar Path, Exchange Student, Ballymackney, Littlepacer and Sophia Royale — are all hold-up or midfield types, and with more closers than the track can naturally accommodate, several will be shuffled wider and further back than ideal, compromising their position. With a lone leader setting an honest but uncontested pace, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine late turn of foot who can find clear daylight on a one-bend 6f circuit, and also rewards the prominent runner if the tempo is soft enough to leave them full of running entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tatianna Leads Untouched
scenarios.trigger: If Tatianna dictates an uncontested, even gallop and the field fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Tatianna bowls along at her own pace with Woodlawn Lily as her nearest pursuer, and the lack of genuine pressure means she is never asked a real question until too late; her Good-ground form and prior win at the trip are key assets.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Tatianna and Woodlawn Lily both travel strongly and open a decisive lead that the hold-up horses cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: The two prominent-style runners effectively run the closers out of the race by the 2f marker, leaving the rear of the field too much ground to make up on the flat Sligo straight; the winner comes from the front two.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Tatianna's pace is just strong enough to soften her up and a genuine hold-up horse finds a clear run to reel her in.
scenarios.body: A true finisher threads through between the post and the rail in the final furlong as Tatianna ties up marginally; Hi Corbett Court (Good-ground placed form, W J Lee) and Mr Montauk (Dylan Browne McMonagle, placed at the trip) are the likeliest beneficiaries, though both are racing in a compressed midfield and must find room.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and several hold-up types surge simultaneously, producing a scrambled, muddling finish.
scenarios.body: A slow early gallop causes a wall of horses to converge in the straight with interference and tight gaps; the race devolves into a lottery favouring whichever hold-up runner finds the cleanest passage.

watchPoints.text: Tatianna — if she breaks cleanly and sets a comfortable gallop unchallenged, she controls the race from the front and the compressed hold-up field faces a very difficult task bridging the gap on Sligo's flat straight.

Mr Montauk — Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking for a Joseph O'Brien-trained runner who has previously placed on Good ground is a class signal worth noting; if he finds clear daylight from midfield in the straight, he is capable of running well above his OR of 60.

Hi Corbett Court — W J Lee partnering a Twomey runner with genuine Good-ground placed form at 6f is a combination with credibility; watch for him to be delivered with a late run along the rail if room opens.

Woodlawn Lily — as the only other prominent-style runner, her ability to tuck in behind Tatianna and save ground is a significant positional advantage over the hold-up heavy field; if Tatianna fades, she is first in line.

Ballymackney — the significant drop in trip (last ran 8f) combined with new cheekpieces from the Meade yard (4/23 T14) is a combination that can produce a forward move at a price; worth monitoring in the market for any stable confidence.

races.name: Baader - Eddie Carr PBR 2000 Handicap

runners_data.name: Magna Kotcha
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Noel Meade, ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle who adds significant class to the saddle; her form string of 6000 is poor and she has zero wins or placings in similar going across four runs, while a finish-fading flag compounds the concern over her ability to sustain an effort on this track.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Magna Kotcha at least has experience of today's distance and going to draw on, though a rating of 53 and stall 13 suggest she faces a stiff task breaking into the shake-up from midfield.

runners_data.name: Apothic Red
runners_data.note: Fitted with a visor and back after 54 days off for McCourt, she has run respectably in Good-ground 6f company (three placed efforts from six similar-going runs) and her waiting style suits if she can get a clear run through 14 runners; held up from the rear, her natural role is genuine but the volume of closers in this field makes traffic a real risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Apothic Red nevertheless rates clear of his 13 rivals on our figures and has experience over today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall one carrying 141 lb, he sets the standard if reproducing his best.

runners_data.name: Quinn's Charm
runners_data.note: Ten months off the track is a major flag — she has six Good-ground runs but all were over 7f-8f, and stepping back to 6f for trainer Mulvany after such a layoff on this tight track asks considerable questions; natural hold-up style, tongue tie fitted, and she needs to show her 6f stamina is sufficient before this run can be taken at face value.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Quinn's Charm none the less has experience over today's trip and going, and her rating puts her firmly in contention at a competitive weight of 139 lb — the chief concern is a 334-day absence.

runners_data.name: Unfamiliar
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good just three days ago and is back quickly; carries a finish-fading note yet recorded a win and a place across ten Good-ground outings, and her hold-up profile actually suits the anticipated race shape if she recovers from that fast turnaround — the recency of her form is a clear positive among this largely out-of-form field.
runners_data.comment: Unfamiliar showed she can win, landing a victory three starts back, but has been unplaced in her last two outings and returns just three days later; she has run over today's trip and going, though her rating of 54 leaves her with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who won over 6f Good and placed three times in 11 similar-going starts, but is shown in midfield because the field is saturated with closers who cannot all get to the back — in reality she is likely to push forward and race closer than her map position suggests; tongue piece and cheekpieces fitted, 11 days since last run, and that natural forward movement makes her one of the most interesting tactical watches.

**Glen Breeze** bounced back to win two starts back, though a sixth last time out tempers expectations; he has experience over today's trip and going, returns fit on 11 days' rest, but carries 137 lb from stall 11 and our rating of 54 leaves him up against it in a 14-runner field.

runners_data.name: Dubai Opulence
runners_data.note: Finish-fading flag attached and a form line of 9-0046 shows limited progression for Lupini; she is a genuine hold-up type shuffled onto the map at midfield given the glut of closers, and three placings from six Good runs suggest she finds a level without winning — STYLE_FIT note means her chance in any scenario demanding a specific position should be tempered.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dubai Opulence at least showed some improvement with a fourth two runs back, and he has experience of today's distance and going; 133 lb from stall 14 makes life harder, though his rating of 53 suggests limited scope to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Countertop
runners_data.note: Finish-fading closer for Mulvany who has been running over 8f-10f for much of her career — this 6f trip looks sharp enough to be a concern, and her Good-ground record shows consistent mid-division finishes rather than any winning threat; shifted onto the map at midfield from her natural hold-up berth, and the combination of trip doubt and redistribution makes her difficult to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts with three unplaced efforts in that sequence, Countertop is hard to fancy on these figures, ranked last of the field; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 16 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Jampa Ling
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and race-shaper; has run exclusively over 6f on Good at this trip and has a placed effort to show (3/6f/GOO) but her overall record is modest with no wins — her value here is entirely tactical as the pace-setter, and her STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 reflects that she is mapped as prominent rather than full lead, though she appears most likely to dominate early.
runners_data.comment: Jampa Ling shaped with promise when third four starts back and returns here fit on a quick 12-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going and a rating of 60 working in his favour — the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and has to shoulder 132 lb from stall 10.

runners_data.name: The Love Machine
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combo is the same person (Sean Davis), which is relatively rare and worth noting; this is a true hold-up type moved to midfield on the map, having won over 5f Soft earlier in her career, and her Good-ground record of one win from 15 runs suggests she needs conditions to fall perfectly — 47 days off adds an element of freshness but also fitness doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and unplaced in five of them, The Love Machine heads here 47 days off the track, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 55 offers some encouragement from stall 6 carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Luminessa
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, so fitness is clearly not an issue, but back-to-back outings on a career form line of 745708 raises the question of quality ceiling; fitted with tongue tie and visor, she is a natural closer repositioned onto the map at midfield due to field saturation, and her best efforts (5th twice on Standard) came on a different surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and back just two days later, Luminessa has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 55 suggests she holds claims — but an eighth last time out and the quick turnaround are the key concerns.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.note: Finish-fading closer for Hourigan who has placed once in four Good-ground runs but has not threatened a win; her form of -00058 shows a modest 8th last time, and being a hold-up type in a field of hold-up types with 35 days between runs means she needs a perfect trip that this congested race shape is unlikely to gift.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with a string of unplaced efforts, She's On The Ball is hard to fancy at the foot of the ratings, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a return to form isn't impossible from stall five.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: McGuinness has a strong 2/26 trainer strike rate over 14 days and Beau Army has placed twice in 15 Good-ground efforts including a third over 8f; fitted with a hood, he is a natural closer who has been moved onto the map at midfield, but his pedigree of placing at longer trips on Good suggests he could show up at a live price if the race is contested and a gap appears.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 13 of 14 on our figures, Beau Army faces a stiff ask here, though she does bring a third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going to the table.

runners_data.name: Windsor Lily
runners_data.note: Finish-fading closer fitted with a blinker who has placed just twice in six Good-ground starts, both on 6f — she has form on this course surface and trip but has been running over 7f lately; moved to midfield from a natural hold-up role, and Murphy's runner deserves respect on course-form alone even if the finishing profile is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Windsor Lily has struggled for consistency and ranks 12th of 14 on our figures, making her hard to fancy here; she does have experience over today's trip and going, and 25 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Sand Art
runners_data.note: Blinker-fitted closer whose form of -87700 shows progressive deterioration, and she has been tried over 10f earlier in the year suggesting 6f may be her sharpest possible trip rather than a comfortable one; Coleman's runner is another genuine hold-up type absorbed into the midfield map position, and finish-fading combined with no wins or places from seven Good-ground starts makes her the hardest to recommend tactically.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sand Art does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 25 days between runs leaves him fresh; but a sequence of unplaced finishes makes it hard to fancy him escaping midfield from stall two.

races.paceDynamic: Jampa Ling is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 6f handicap and, with no natural rival likely to push them hard from the gates, sets up to control a steady, unchallenged gallop on Good turf at Sligo. The rest of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Glen Breeze, Dubai Opulence, Countertop, The Love Machine, Luminessa, She's On The Ball, Beau Army, Windsor Lily and Sand Art are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is nowhere else to put them; of those, Glen Breeze (a proven 6f winner here in style on Good) and Dubai Opulence are most likely to push furthest forward in reality, but neither is a natural front-runner. With Jampa Ling dictating a controlled pace and a wall of hold-up horses queuing behind, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel just off the pace and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — a one-dimensional waiting ride from deep in a field of 14 over a tight 6f track is a low-percentage strategy here, making the handful of horses capable of tracking the leader from close range the most advantaged profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jampa Ling Controls, Closers Charge
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling dictates a genuine but not suicidal pace and the field fans wide in the straight, horses tracking in second to fifth positions mow them down.
scenarios.body: Jampa Ling sets an honest but sustainable tempo, leaving the race set up for those who have tracked within two lengths and can quicken on the flat Good ground over the final furlong; the compact Sligo straight rewards the horse who picks up earliest rather than the one who arrives latest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Hold
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling goes too steady and the pack stacks up behind, creating a traffic lottery, the race is decided by those with the best position and a clean run.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race over 6f on Good ground can gift the lead horse a winning advantage if the closers are blocked or forced wide in a bunched finish; Jampa Ling and any horse that boldly moves up to sit second or third by halfway will be hardest to catch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Hotting Up, Stragglers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If more of the redistributed horses contest the early positions than expected, creating a genuinely contested pace, the race opens up for a late finisher tracking widest.
scenarios.body: A busier early pace would burn off Jampa Ling sooner than usual and compress finishing positions, giving the horse who settles last and produces the widest, unimpeded run a narrow window; this is the scenario where a true hold-up horse benefits, but the sheer volume of similarly-minded runners makes a clean late run hard to find.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Checks, Gaps Appear
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling causes interference mid-race and several fancied runners lose momentum, a fresh-enough horse with positional flexibility lands it.
scenarios.body: A messy race with 14 runners squeezed into Sligo's tight 6f favours the horse who either avoids trouble entirely or has the raw ability to overcome it; lower-rated horses with something to prove on a career-best going figure become live each-way threats.

watchPoints.text: Jampa Ling controls all pace — if she gets a soft lead unchallenged into the Sligo straight, even modest late runners will face a bigger task than their form suggests, and the pace dynamic could be far more compressed than a 14-runner field implies.

Glen Breeze is a genuine 6f Good-ground winner at this level and her natural instinct to race forward means she may bypass her mapped midfield slot entirely — watch the first two furlongs to see if she pushes up to track Jampa Ling, which would immediately make her the primary pace threat.

Unfamiliar ran just three days ago and returns here quickly; if she travels sweetly from hold-up and her fitness holds from that recent run, she represents the most current form in the field — but monitor her early in the race for any signs of a horse who has left her run in the paddock.

With nine or more genuine hold-up horses in a 14-runner field over Sligo's tight 6f, traffic congestion in the final two furlongs is almost inevitable — any horse drawn wide or forced to switch late will lose significant ground, making draw and early positioning critical to assess from the stalls.

Beau Army's trainer Adrian McGuinness holds a 2/26 strike rate over the last 14 days, a modest but active yard; with a hood fitted and a horse who has placed on Good ground, watch for Reese Holohan (7lb claim) to try to secure a position closer to the pace than the map suggests.

races.name: Guinness Handicap

runners_data.name: Chicago Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good recently, holds strong prominent claims stepping up to 1m5½f; W J Lee is a key booking, similar-going form reads 2 wins from 5, and this is the main pace threat to Mare Crisium from just off the lead.
runners_data.comment: Chicago Moon bounced back to winning ways last time out and, having run over today's going before, she arrives in good heart 23 days on. Carrying 140 lb is the one query, but on her best recent form she is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner here; Max Popan (10lb claimer) takes the mount but the key asset is a clear lead with no rival to pressure her, and Good ground suits — form is modest but the pace role itself is the angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mare Crisium nevertheless carries strong positives — she has experience over today's going, is fit from a run 16 days ago, and our rating puts her third-best in this field; the concern is that consistency has eluded her, with no finish better than fourth in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a win over 17f on Good and a fade-in-finish flag to note; Gavin Ryan is a quality booking and the trip is well within range, but a slow pace from Mare Crisium makes it hard for him to land his challenge off a steady gallop.
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning ways last time out, but three unplaced efforts before that temper enthusiasm; Private Larry has experience on today's going and faces a competitive field carrying 137 lb, leaving him a tough ask from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes rides this hold-up type from Gordon Elliott's yard, though the yard's T14 ratio is modest; only one run on similar going (7th/12f/STA), form reads as lightly raced and largely unexposed, so potential exists but pace shape doesn't suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Sonny Corleone brings some going experience but the trainer's recent strike rate of just 4% gives little confidence, and a career-high 137 lb is a stiff ask for a horse rated 63.

runners_data.name: Cascade Canyon
runners_data.note: DBM takes the ride on this hold-up runner who has faded in recent finishes; 47 days off the track and a 0-from-5 record on similar going are concerns, and the mapped midfield position reflects redistribution rather than his natural rear-of-field preference.
runners_data.comment: Cascade Canyon has going experience to call on and our rating of 67 makes him a leading threat here, with a fourth three starts back hinting at better than his recent ninth suggests — yet winless in his last five starts, that inconsistency remains the key concern.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Astolat
runners_data.note: Placed over 14f on Good last time, showing stamina is not an issue; her true style is hold-up but the overcrowded rear forces her into a midfield slot she may not relish — the style-fit discount (0.90) is warranted though her best form is over this kind of trip.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last two starts, Queen Of Astolat arrives here in improving recent form and has experience of today's trip and conditions — our rating of 65, fourth-best of the eleven, puts her right in the mix; the risk is that she's winless in recent starts and must shoulder 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Grey Intentions
runners_data.note: 68 days since last run is a notable freshness question, and three fades-in-finish flags compound the concern; a natural hold-up type pushed into midfield by field congestion, this horse's Good-ground record is mediocre (4-from-5 in the top half) and the pace map doesn't help.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts and absent 68 days, Grey Intentions does arrive with going experience on her side, though a career-best effort is needed if she is to make her mark from a midfield ranking.

runners_data.name: Ellens Bay
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced (three runs, all poor) and the redistribution from hold-up to midfield is largely academic given a bare form reading of 0-00; Luke McAteer rides for a trainer with a small yard, and this trip is uncharted territory — hard to be enthusiastic.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Ellens Bay faces a stiff ask here; the trainer's current 1/21 spell offers little encouragement, though she has run over today's going before and returns after a 36-day break.

runners_data.name: Elzaam Express
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell sends this hold-up runner out after 61 days off; all three runs have been on Good ground at 10f, so stepping up to 1m5½f is a significant unknown and the fade-in-finish flag is a warning — midfield by map position but naturally a rear runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — all unplaced bar a fifth — Elzaam Express returns after 61 days with a trainer in desperate form (0/36 over 14 days), and ranked last on our figures; experience over today's going is the sole crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Curious Jane
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy double-books with Ellens Bay (different jockeys); Rory Mulligan's 5lb claim is an asset in weight terms but this horse carries a fade flag, a 0-from-5 record on similar going, and is 16 days since last run — the midfield slot is redistribution, not natural habitat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Curious Jane faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's going before, but a trainer operating at just 5% in the last 14 days offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Canon Law
runners_data.note: Freshest recent profile of the hold-up brigade — five runs in similar going, consistently placed 5th-6th, and 12 days since last run for Brendan Duke's yard (T14: 2/5); Rory Cleary rides and the 43 OR is lowest in the field, though the style-fit note (0.92) is the most favourable of the redistributed group.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but ran second two starts back, showing he's capable of mixing it; has run over today's going before and returns just 12 days after his latest outing, though an official mark of 43 leaves him with plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Mare Crisium is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 1m5½f handicap and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she is set to dictate at a sustainable gallop from the outset on Good turf at Sligo. Chicago Moon is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely track her just off the pace, giving the race a clear two-tier early shape with a lone leader and one close follower. The remainder of the field — Private Larry, Sonny Corleone, Cascade Canyon, Queen Of Astolat, Grey Intentions, Ellens Bay, Elzaam Express, Curious Jane and Canon Law — are all hold-up or midfield types, with several redistributed to midfield on the pace map because the field simply contains more closers than natural positions available at the rear; Queen Of Astolat, Grey Intentions and Ellens Bay are among those most likely to be shuffled up rather than dropping out the back as they would naturally prefer. A controlled, unhurried pace set by Mare Crisium with only Chicago Moon for company in the early stages strongly favours prominent racers who can dictate or travel smoothly into the race, and the hold-up runners face the twin risk of a steady gallop yielding no late run and a messy midfield traffic situation.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium bowls along uncontested and the steady pace produces a flat-out finish from the front.
scenarios.body: Mare Crisium sets every fraction on her own terms, conserving energy through the long 1m5½f trip and kicking clear when challenged in the straight; a sustainable pace on Good ground suits a front-runner who can find a second effort without having been burned up early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium's lead is modest enough that Chicago Moon tracks her comfortably and picks her off in the straight.
scenarios.body: Chicago Moon, prominent throughout and fresh off a win at this trip in similar going, holds a stylistic advantage over a field of hold-up types who need a strong pace that isn't materialising; W J Lee can time the challenge perfectly from second position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium goes faster than expected and the pace genuinely collapses late enough for closers to reel her in.
scenarios.body: A true collapse of the leader in the final two furlongs could allow the best-credentialled hold-up horse to emerge from the pack, with Private Larry's winning form over 12f on Good and Canon Law's consistent placed efforts in similar conditions making them the likeliest beneficiaries; the redistributed nature of most closers here, however, limits the probability of a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded midfield produces traffic problems and a muddled finish where no single style dominates.
scenarios.body: With so many natural hold-up types compressed into midfield and racing out of their preferred role, interference or a bunched finish is a genuine risk; in that scenario, the horse best placed to thread through — most likely one with the highest OR and strongest recent form like Chicago Moon or Private Larry — benefits from others being blocked.

watchPoints.text: Mare Crisium (sole front-runner) — watch whether Max Popan settles her at a genuine solo clip or crawls; if she barely breaks stride, the pace collapses and prominent types like Chicago Moon inherit the race without a true test.

Chicago Moon — W J Lee's positioning in the opening quarter-mile is critical; if he sits too far back behind a traffic-jammed midfield rather than locking onto Mare Crisium's quarters, he loses his natural advantage as the only genuine prominent runner.

Private Larry — Gavin Ryan will need to find a clear run from hold-up, but with up to eight horses bunched in midfield this horse's fade-in-finish flag and need for a strong tempo make a winning run dependent on things going right in the straight.

Grey Intentions, Ellens Bay and Elzaam Express — all three are redistributed hold-up types carrying fade flags and significant gaps since their last run (68d, 36d, 61d respectively); watch for any of them to drift wide seeking room, which could disrupt the midfield order in the final turn.

Cascade Canyon with Dylan Browne McMonagle — despite a poor recent record, DBM rarely takes bad rides without a reason; watch market moves to see if a yard whisper backs this hold-up runner despite the 47-day absence and fade flag.

races.name: Rockshore Cider Handicap

runners_data.name: Charlie Brow'n
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has been well beaten in recent outings at 12f on Good; stepping up to 1m5½f is a potential plus but 181 days off the track is a significant concern and there is no winning form on similar ground in recent history.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and experience over today's trip and going in his favour, Charlie Brow'n looks a leading danger carrying 142 lb; the chief concern is a 181-day absence, which leaves fitness the key question.

runners_data.name: Reflectionist
runners_data.note: Genuine closer who has a win over 13f on Good ground to his name, but a warning flag for fading late is a real concern in a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo; 16 days since last run is fine, and the apprentice booking is noted.
runners_data.comment: Reflectionist won last time out to arrive here in form, and has run over today's trip and going before, but three unplaced efforts in the four starts preceding that victory give the overall picture a patchy look at a competitive 60 mark.

runners_data.name: Young Churchill
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a place at 12f on Good in recent form, but his record at longer distances is patchy and his last five runs include a soft-ground effort over 20f that weakened late; needs a strong pace to deliver his best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Young Churchill nonetheless shaped with promise when third two runs back, and he returns here after 21 days off having run over today's trip and going before — his rating of 73 makes him one to note at the weights carrying 142 lb.

runners_data.name: God The Highness
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's yard has been active with 4 winners from 31 in the last 14 days, which is a positive stable flag; hold-up style suits a strong pace but this will be a steady tempo, and his Going record here is solid enough to consider.

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on Good and placed at the same distance, so the trip and conditions are genuinely in his favour; however, this is a horse whose natural role is off the pace, and squeezed into a midfield position rather than his preferred closing berth, his chance is somewhat compromised by the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Eastern Wind does at least own a second three starts back to suggest she retains some ability, though eighth and sixth since then are harder to ignore; carrying 136 lb on today's trip and going she has experienced before, she appeals as a midfield proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Think About It
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up type who has been absent 86 days and whose best form at this distance has been on softer ground; racing out of his natural backmarker position due to the volume of hold-up horses in this field, which further dims his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and not seen out for 86 days, Think About It returns with plenty to prove; she has run over today's going before, but a burden of 136 lb makes life harder still for a filly ranked ninth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Deluca Chop
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, wearing a visor and wearing the form 233211 to advertise his current well-being; 46 days between runs is straightforward, and the STYLE_FIT flag here reflects that he is mapped as prominent but in truth he is the horse who dictates — his role is exactly right for this race shape, making him the central tactical figure.
runners_data.comment: Deluca Chop has winning form in his last six starts — a winner last time out and two starts back — though 46 days off the track is a fitness query, and his ranking of 12th in the field gives him plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 12f on Good and twice on Standard, so the track conditions are not a concern; though naturally a hold-up horse, the field congestion means he is mapped to midfield, and if he can tuck in just behind the leader he is likely racing closer to the front than usual — his recent form 134022 shows consistent placing.
runners_data.comment: Without Love has placed four times in his last six starts — second on each of his two most recent outings — but ranked 14th of 17 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask against stronger company here, however his current form and going experience offer slim crumbs of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: McCourt-trained hold-up specialist with a placed effort over 18f on Good, suggesting the stamina is there; squeezed into midfield from his preferred backmarker role by the sheer volume of hold-up horses, and the STYLE_FIT caveat applies — he needs a strong pace and clear daylight which this shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Maxwell Smart does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 24 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh — though 132 lb and an official rating of 50 make it hard to see him threatening from midfield.

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-strap and cheekpieces, which is worth noting as a potential headgear angle; hold-up style pushed into midfield due to field composition, and recent form at 13-16f on Good shows mid-table finishes without a win — needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Mystic Rose arrives here 24 days fresh and has run over today's trip and going, though she remains yet to win in her last six starts — a third last time out offers mild encouragement, but a pair of fifths and a seventh in between tempers expectations for this lightly tested filly.

runners_data.name: Wungudi
runners_data.note: Has been off 273 days, which is the longest absence in the field and a significant flag; flagged for fading in the finish and mapped away from her natural backmarker position, making this a tough assignment on return from a lengthy layoff.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and returning after a 273-day absence, Wungudi faces a stiff ask ranked 13 of 17 on our figures; a ninth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Anightaway
runners_data.note: 128 days off the track and a form string reading 000-08 tells a blunt story; tongue-strap fitted, flags for fading late, and now asked to race out of his natural hold-up role — very hard to make a case here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning from a 128-day absence, Anightaway is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked last of the 17 runners — though he has run over today's going before and that offers a slim foothold.

runners_data.name: Piatra Neamt
runners_data.note: Trained by the same yard as Deluca Chop (S M Duffy), which is worth flagging as a potential stable companion dynamic; form 60-005 is modest, flagged for fading, and a 79-day gap between runs adds to the query marks around fitness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Piatra Neamt faces a stiff ask after 79 days off; going experience at least counts in her favour, but her recent record offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: Three-pound claimer Wesley Joyce takes the ride, which is an apprentice booking worth monitoring in a big field; recent form at 16f on Good showed a fifth, so the trip is not unfamiliar, but fades late and is not in his natural position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than seventh in recent outings, Plus Or Minus cuts a frustrating figure; he does have experience over today's trip and conditions, but ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, it's hard to make a compelling case.

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: No jockey declared in the data, which is itself a minor concern for race-day planning; form 170009 is erratic, flagged for late fading, and the Good ground record is poor across a substantial sample — hard to fancy from off the pace in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Autocrat's win six starts back gives him a proven winning benchmark, and he arrives on a sharp 16-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going — our rating of 75 marks him as the top-rated runner in the field; the risk is his unplaced efforts in the interim.

runners_data.name: Kings Gesture
runners_data.note: No jockey declared, form reads 5-8000, and the horse is flagged for fading late; natural hold-up style displaced to midfield here and the record on Good or Standard ground offers almost no encouragement — a long-shot scenario only.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kings Gesture carries 132 lb off an official mark of 50, though our rating of 62 suggests he retains more ability than recent unplaced efforts imply; a return to form could see him competitive here.

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: Slattery yard has been firing with 5 from 41 in 14 days — a busy and live stable; hold-up style means this horse is also in a compromised position in this race shape, but recent form 047-06 over middle distances on Good and Standard shows some resilience that makes him one of the more interesting of the closing pack if the pace lifts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Preparations has nonetheless shown enough in recent form to command respect — she has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 65 suggests she holds untapped potential. The risk is that a fourth is her best recent finish.

races.paceDynamic: Deluca Chop is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine pace rival to press him — he can dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop from the front over this 1m5½f trip on Good ground at Sligo. With one horse controlling the pace and no rival willing or able to challenge him for the lead, the tempo is likely to be steady early before Deluca Chop's connections ask him to quicken, a pattern consistent with his recent form string of 233211. The field is saturated with hold-up types — Eastern Wind, Think About It, Without Love, Maxwell Smart, Mystic Rose, Wungudi, Anightaway, Piatra Neamt, Plus Or Minus, Autocrat, Kings Gesture and others are all genuine closers who have been mapped forward simply because there is no room for all of them at the rear — meaning the pack will compress in midfield and the closing kick from the back may be blunted by traffic. This race shape strongly favours Deluca Chop to control and convert from the front, with a secondary advantage for any horse that can track him prominently in the early stages without burning fuel, as the congested midfield pack will be racing out of role and fighting for clear runs in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Deluca Chop Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Deluca Chop breaks cleanly and settles into an uncontested lead, dictating a measured pace over the 1m5½f trip.
scenarios.body: With no pace rival to press him, Deluca Chop can conserve energy through the early stages and deploy his finishing effort on his own terms, exactly the scenario his recent 233211 form suggests he thrives in. Horses with prominent early positions who can track him without overextending will be best placed, while the congested closers will face the twin problems of traffic and a pace that never truly collapsed into a true test.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Deluca Chop's pace is genuinely sustainable but just strong enough that a horse tracking in second or third can produce a decisive late kick to overhaul him.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting two to three lengths off the leader throughout has the best of both worlds — the tactical position is secure and the closing run is shorter than any hold-up rival's.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Navigate Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and the front-runner ties up in the final furlong, opening the door for hold-up horses who find a clear run.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield will make this extremely difficult to execute cleanly, as many of the redistributed hold-up types are not in their natural position and will need luck in running to produce a finishing burst.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Unravels Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a rival challenges Deluca Chop for the lead early, raising the pace materially and setting up a stamina test that benefits a genuine stayer coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong gallop would stretch the field and allow a fresh-legged hold-up horse with proven stamina to pick up the pieces, but this scenario relies on a pace scenario the runner data does not strongly support.

watchPoints.text: Deluca Chop breaks cleanly and is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead — watch whether any rival attempts to press him in the first three furlongs, because if none do, the race is effectively over as a pace contest.

The compressed midfield of redistributed hold-up horses — Eastern Wind, Maxwell Smart, Without Love, Think About It and others — will likely cause significant bunching on the turn into the straight; watch for crowding and horses losing momentum on the final bend.

Reflectionist is flagged for fading in the finish and has a record of 10th, 10th and 11th in his last three turf runs of 16f or more on Good — the step back up in trip is not obviously in his favour despite a recent win at 13f.
Stable companion dynamic between Deluca Chop and Piatra Neamt (both S M Duffy) in the same race — worth monitoring market moves on both runners in the hour before post time.
Three horses (Autocrat, Kings Gesture) have no declared jockey in the available data — confirm riders at the overnight declaration stage as late bookings could signal market-relevant information.
